title: Jezero Margin Unit: what should be investigated next?

site.name: Margin Unit (marginal carbonates)
site.description: A carbonate-bearing unit along the inner margin of Jezero crater, near the western delta. Jezero crater is 47.52 km across and centred at 18.41° N, 77.69° E (planetocentric, east-positive) in the USGS Gazetteer (MDIM 2.1 control network).

citations.quote: Diameter 47.52 km Center Latitude 18.41 ° Center Longitude 77.69 °
we identify a distinct carbonate-bearing unit, the “Marginal Carbonates,” located along the inner margin of the crater, near the largest inlet valley and the western delta.

observations.title: Distinct carbonate-bearing unit along the inner margin (CRISM)
observations.statement: Orbital CRISM hyperspectral images, used with high-resolution imagery and digital elevation models, identify a distinct carbonate-bearing unit (the “Marginal Carbonates”) along the inner margin of Jezero crater, near the largest inlet valley and the western delta.

citations.quote: Using orbital visible/near-infrared hyperspectral images from the Compact Reconnaissance Imaging Spectrometer for Mars (CRISM) along with high resolution imagery and digital elevation models, we identify a distinct carbonate-bearing unit, the “Marginal Carbonates,” located along the inner margin of the crater, near the largest inlet valley and the western delta.

observations.title: Crater-wide MRO mineral map: carbonate and olivine
observations.statement: A colour-coded image of Jezero made from MRO CRISM and CTX data shows carbonates (green) and olivine sand (red), which the caption describes as eroding out of carbonate-containing rocks.

citations.quote: The green color represents minerals called carbonates, which are especially good at preserving fossilized life on Earth. Red represents olivine sand eroding out of carbonate-containing rocks.

observations.curationNote: Regional context: the caption describes minerals across Jezero crater and does not identify the margin unit, so this is not counted as a direct margin-unit observation.

observations.title: Upper etched unit (Nue) mapped along the interior margin and across Nili Planum
observations.statement: Geologic mapping on a CTX base mosaic describes an upper etched unit (Nue) occurring along the northern crater rim and wall, along the interior margin of Jezero crater, and throughout Nili Planum; the map associates it with olivine and variable carbonate, citing earlier orbital studies.

citations.quote: Upper etched unit—Indurated, rugged, moderately cratered to heavily cratered, light- to intermediate-toned unit located along and on the northern Jezero crater rim and wall, along the interior margin of Jezero crater, and throughout Nili Planum.
citations.locator: Map sheet, Description of Map Units (Nue)

citations.quote: Associated with olivine and variable carbonate
citations.locator: Map sheet, Description of Map Units (Nue)

observations.curationNote: Regional context, reclassified in M3. SIM 3464 defines Nue as a regional unit (crater rim and wall, interior margin, Nili Planum) and never uses the term “margin unit”. Nue overlaps the interior margin geographically, but no source in this dataset equates Nue with the margin unit, so it is not treated as a direct observation of the margin unit.

observations.title: First abrasion of a rock in the marginal carbonate unit
observations.statement: Perseverance arrived at Mandu Wall and abraded a rock within the marginal carbonate unit (the Amherst Point abrasion patch), giving the first look beneath a margin-unit rock surface.

citations.quote: This week on Mars, Perseverance officially kicked off the Margin Campaign by arriving at Mandu Wall and performing the first abrasion of a rock within the marginal carbonate unit!
In this Sol 915 (September 16, 2023) Navcam image, Perseverance looks down at the Amherst Point abrasion patch, catching the first subsurface glimpse at a rock in the marginal carbonate unit.

observations.curationNote: Not linked to any gap: the source describes imaging of the abrasion, not a compositional measurement.

observations.title: Hydrated silica reported in the Lefroy Bay sample
observations.statement: A team member reports that Sample 23 (Lefroy Bay), collected from the Turquoise Bay rock on the margin unit, showed the presence of hydrated silica.

citations.quote: Sample 23 is called "Lefroy Bay," and we collected it from the "Turquoise Bay" rock on the margin unit
One of the things we saw was the presence of hydrated silica. The exciting thing about hydrated silica is that on Earth it has the highest potential to preserve biosignatures.

observations.title: Comet Geyser core appears to be mainly carbonate and silica
observations.statement: The Comet Geyser rock core, collected at the Bunsen Peak workspace in the Margin Unit, appears to be composed primarily of carbonate and silica.

citations.quote: at the Bunsen Peak workspace deep within the Margin Unit

Although this rock’s origin remains under investigation and the rover team continues to explore different hypotheses, this core is particularly exciting because it appears to be composed primarily of two minerals: carbonate and silica.

observations.title: SHERLOC detects hydrated carbonates (Pelican Point)
observations.statement: SHERLOC spectra of the Pelican Point sample's rock show peaks assigned to hydrated and non-hydrated carbonates and hydrated sulfates, the first detection of hydrated carbonates in Jezero crater.

citations.quote: SHERLOC spectra contain peaks that can be assigned to hydrated and non-hydrated carbonates and hydrated sulfates. This is the first time that hydrated carbonates have been detected in Jezero crater.
Campaign: Margin Region of Interest: Mandu Wall

observations.title: PIXL: silica-rich areas and carbonate-bearing Fe-Mg material (Castle Geyser)
observations.statement: PIXL analyses of the Castle Geyser abrasion (the Comet Geyser core's rock) show almost entirely silica-rich areas and Fe-Mg material containing both carbonate and silicates, with scattered Ca-sulfate and Ti-chromite.

citations.quote: PIXL analyses show that Castle Geyser consists almost entirely of silica-rich areas and Fe-Mg material containing both carbonate and silicates, with scattered Ca-sulfate and Ti-chromite, and possible NaCl.
Campaign: Margin Region of Interest: Western Margin

interpretations.title: Lake carbonates formed near the shore
interpretations.claim: The Marginal Carbonates may preserve authigenic lacustrine carbonates, precipitated in the near-shore environment of the Jezero paleolake.

citations.quote: Based on their strong carbonate signatures, topographic properties, and location in the crater, we propose that this unit may preserve authigenic lacustrine carbonates, precipitated in the near-shore environment of the Jezero paleolake.

interpretations.title: Mineral carbonation of olivine-bearing rock
interpretations.claim: Presented as an alternative to a lakeshore origin: the carbonates formed through mineral carbonation, in which silicate minerals such as olivine react with CO₂ and are converted to carbonates.
interpretations.attributedTo: E. Gibbons, NASA Perseverance blog (2023), stating an alternative hypothesis

citations.quote: An alternative hypothesis is that the carbonates formed through mineral carbonation, where silicate minerals (like olivine) react with CO₂ and are converted to carbonates.

interpretations.title: Regional unit Nue interpreted as volcanic ash-fall or pyroclastic drape
interpretations.claim: Sun & Stack interpret the olivine-bearing upper etched unit (Nue) as ash-fall or pyroclastic-surge deposits, based on its draping morphology and banding, and note that it may not have been affected by lacustrine processes.
interpretations.attributedTo: Sun & Stack (2020), USGS SIM 3464, citing Kremer et al. (2019) and Mandon et al. (2020)

citations.quote: We therefore interpreted unit Nue, and unit Nle by proxy, as ash-fall or pyroclastic-surge deposits due to the draping morphology and banding observed in unit Nue
occurs along the Jezero crater walls and in Nili Planum, and may not have been affected by lacustrine processes like unit Nle.

interpretations.curationNote: Regional context, reclassified in M3. This interprets the regional unit Nue, not a named margin unit, so before 2024-08-30 it is not a competing hypothesis for the margin unit in this dataset. From 2024-08-30 the Mars 2020 team lists a volcanic (pyroclastic) origin as a hypothesis for the margin unit itself; that hypothesis links to this record as context only.

interpretations.title: Sedimentary origin (Mars 2020 working hypothesis)
interpretations.claim: The margin unit is sedimentary in origin; one of three hypotheses the Mars 2020 team reports carrying for the unit.
interpretations.attributedTo: Mars 2020 science team, as reported by K. Stack Morgan (NASA blog, 2024)

citations.quote: a thought-provoking series of presentations that tackled the three hypotheses we’re carrying for the origin of this unit: sedimentary, volcanic (pyroclastic), or crystalline igneous.

interpretations.title: Volcanic (pyroclastic) origin (Mars 2020 working hypothesis)
interpretations.claim: The margin unit is volcanic (pyroclastic) in origin; one of three hypotheses the Mars 2020 team reports carrying for the unit.
interpretations.attributedTo: Mars 2020 science team, as reported by K. Stack Morgan (NASA blog, 2024)

citations.quote: a thought-provoking series of presentations that tackled the three hypotheses we’re carrying for the origin of this unit: sedimentary, volcanic (pyroclastic), or crystalline igneous.

interpretations.curationNote: Linked to SIM 3464's regional Nue interpretation as context only; the regional record is not counted as local support.

interpretations.title: Crystalline igneous origin (Mars 2020 working hypothesis)
interpretations.claim: The margin unit is crystalline igneous in origin; one of three hypotheses the Mars 2020 team reports carrying for the unit.
interpretations.attributedTo: Mars 2020 science team, as reported by K. Stack Morgan (NASA blog, 2024)

citations.quote: a thought-provoking series of presentations that tackled the three hypotheses we’re carrying for the origin of this unit: sedimentary, volcanic (pyroclastic), or crystalline igneous.

interpretations.title: Silica-cemented sandstone (Pelican Point)
interpretations.claim: The Pelican Point sample is tentatively interpreted as a silica-cemented medium to coarse sandstone that experienced aqueous alteration.

citations.quote: Pelican Point is tentatively interpreted here to be a silica-cemented medium to coarse sandstone that experienced aqueous alteration.

interpretations.title: Altered intrusive igneous rock (Comet Geyser)
interpretations.claim: Alternatively, Comet Geyser could be an intrusive mafic to ultramafic igneous rock, highly altered by fluids, and the same origin could apply to the two earlier Margin samples. Whether it is igneous or sedimentary remains undetermined.

citations.quote: Alternatively, Comet Geyser could be an intrusive mafic to ultramafic igneous rock, highly altered by interaction with fluids. In retrospect, the same origin could also apply to the two previous Margin samples.
Whether Comet Geyser is a carbonated ultramafic igneous rock (e.g., a listvenite) or a cemented and altered sedimentary rock remains undetermined.

gaps.title: Link to the lake
gaps.question: Are the carbonates along Jezero's inner margin related to the lake?

citations.quote: it is unclear whether or not the carbonates in Jezero are related to the lacustrine activity.

priority.statement: Horgan et al. state that whether the carbonates are lacustrine is critical for evaluating the site's astrobiological potential.

citations.quote: This distinction is critical for evaluating the astrobiological potential of the site

gaps.curationNote: Competing hypotheses: the lacustrine proposal (Horgan et al. 2020) and the mineral-carbonation alternative (2023); each counts only once published.

gaps.title: How the margin rocks formed
gaps.question: How did the margin rocks, and the carbonate within them, form?

citations.quote: Although we don’t yet know exactly how the margin rocks, or the carbonate within them formed, the team is eager to drill into these rocks and unlock their secrets.

priority.statement: The NASA blog describes the margin carbonate unit as pivotal in selecting Jezero as the landing site.

citations.quote: a special rock unit that played a pivotal role in selecting Jezero as the landing site for exploration

gaps.title: No rover measurement yet
gaps.question: Has any rover measurement of margin-unit composition been made?

origin.rule: Open while every local observation supporting the competing hypotheses is orbital; addressed once a rover compositional measurement of margin-unit rock is published.

gaps.curationNote: Dated from 2019-11-11, the first margin-unit hypothesis in this dataset, whose only local support is orbital.

gaps.title: Sedimentary or igneous?
gaps.question: Is the margin unit sedimentary, volcanic (pyroclastic), or crystalline igneous in origin?

citations.quote: a thought-provoking series of presentations that tackled the three hypotheses we’re carrying for the origin of this unit: sedimentary, volcanic (pyroclastic), or crystalline igneous.

gaps.title: Origin of the mapped olivine/carbonate units
gaps.question: What are the origin and complete mineralogy of the olivine- and carbonate-bearing map units? The map authors say this needs rover instruments and returned samples.

citations.quote: Confirming the origins of these units and their complete mineralogy will ultimately require analyses from higher resolution instruments on the Perseverance rover and from returned samples

gaps.curationNote: Regional context, reclassified in M3: SIM 3464's “these units” are its regional map units (including Nue and Nle), not explicitly the margin unit. Not counted as a local gap.

assumptions.statement: Task costs and the budget are abstract resource points chosen by the MDI team.
assumptions.rationale: They illustrate trade-offs only; they are not Perseverance or MRO operations figures.

assumptions.statement: For evidence quality, MDI ranks regional context below orbital observations, orbital below rover in-situ measurements, and rover below Earth-laboratory analysis.
assumptions.rationale: MDI methodological assumption: closer, higher-resolution measurements of the target outrank remote or regional ones.

assumptions.statement: The rover can reach and work safely on margin-unit outcrops.
assumptions.rationale: Traverse planning, terrain and hazards are outside this simulation.

assumptions.statement: The named instruments can make the measurements described in each task.
assumptions.rationale: Capabilities are summarised by the MDI team for this simulation, not taken from cited instrument documentation.

assumptions.statement: A sealed core would eventually be analysed in laboratories on Earth.
assumptions.rationale: Sample-return timing and feasibility are not modelled; this task's value depends on this assumption.

assumptions.statement: The orbital camera is available to target the site.
assumptions.rationale: Spacecraft and instrument operating status are not checked in this dataset.

resources.name: Investigation effort
resources.description: Abstract budget standing in for rover time, power and data volume.

tasks.title: Stand-off survey of margin outcrops
tasks.description: Map the composition and texture of margin-unit outcrops from a distance before choosing where to abrade.

addresses.rationale: SuperCam and Mastcam-Z are rover instruments, so a stand-off survey would give rover-based observations of margin-unit rock.
Composition and texture from a survey are inputs to the question of how the margin rocks formed.

tasks.title: Abrade a margin rock and analyse it up close
tasks.description: Remove the weathered surface of a margin-unit rock and measure its fine-scale chemistry, mineralogy and texture.

addresses.rationale: PIXL, SHERLOC and WATSON measure an abraded rock surface from the rover arm.
Fine-scale chemistry, mineralogy and texture of an abraded surface bear directly on how the rock and its carbonate formed.
Fine-scale textures and mineral relationships bear on whether the carbonate precipitated in a lake.

tasks.title: Core a margin-unit sample for Earth laboratories
tasks.description: Collect and seal a rock core so that laboratories on Earth could test its origin in detail.

addresses.rationale: The team states it is eager to drill into these rocks to learn how they formed.

citations.quote: the team is eager to drill into these rocks and unlock their secrets

addresses.rationale: The PDS report states that detailed laboratory study of the grains/clasts would address whether the carbonate is detrital or formed by in-situ alteration.

citations.quote: Detailed laboratory study of the suite of grains/clasts would address this unknown
citations.locator: Comet Geyser initial report (M2020-1088-27), Returned Sample Science Considerations

tasks.title: Targeted HiRISE stereo imaging of margin contacts
tasks.description: Image the contacts between the margin unit and neighbouring units from orbit, to compare draping and shoreline-like geometry.

addresses.rationale: Horgan et al. based the lacustrine proposal partly on topographic properties and location; stereo topography would re-examine that basis.

citations.quote: Based on their strong carbonate signatures, topographic properties, and location in the crater, we propose that this unit may preserve authigenic lacustrine carbonates, precipitated in the near-shore environment of the Jezero paleolake.

limitations: Small curated subset of public sources the MDI build environment could access; key journal articles (e.g. Zastrow & Glotch 2021) could not be read and are not included.
Where a journal's own online date could not be accessed, the USGS Publications Warehouse record date is used.

Verified historical sample locations are displayed on the map (in historical replay, only once their source is public); their coordinate convention is inferred by cross-validation. No verified Margin Unit boundary is available, and simulated observation tasks have not been assigned precise geographic locations.
Task-gap links and the gaps each observation addresses are AI-drafted curation, pending human review; curated scientific judgements (discrimination, priority) are not scored until approved.

outcomes.ifObserved: Laboratory study shows the carbonate occurs as detrital grains

discriminationAssessments.rationale: The PDS report frames the carbonate's origin as either detrital grains or in-situ alteration and says laboratory study would address it; for Comet Geyser it frames the rock as either carbonated ultramafic igneous or cemented, altered sedimentary. Reading 'detrital carbonate' as favoring a sedimentary origin is an inference that needs expert review.

citations.quote: the origin of the carbonate, whether detrital grains or the result of in situ alteration, is still unknown.
citations.locator: Comet Geyser initial report (M2020-1088-27), Returned Sample Science Considerations

citations.quote: Whether Comet Geyser is a carbonated ultramafic igneous rock (e.g., a listvenite) or a cemented and altered sedimentary rock remains undetermined.
